title: An unpaired surrogate in UTF-16 after a byte order mark is an encoding error at its unit, and the mark is not counted
notes: The stream is a UTF-16LE byte order mark (0xFF 0xFE), the characters U+00E9, colon and space, a high surrogate (U+D800) that is followed by the character b instead of a low surrogate, and a line break. A high surrogate must be paired with a low one (section 5.2 names UTF-16 as an allowed encoding), so the stream is refused as an encoding error. The position is the kit rule: the first byte of the ill-formed sequence, with the column counting the characters decoded before it, and the byte order mark is not a character of the text. Three characters come before the surrogate, so it is at 1:4; a reader that counts the mark reports column 5, and one that counts bytes or code units reports a later column.

provenance.reference: Written for the kit to fill a gap: no case fixed the position of an encoding error in a stream that starts with a byte order mark.
